Family history dossier · maternal line · Louth, Lincolnshire → Mackay · Ireland → Queensland Hotel · Gippsland → Tambo Upper

The Jacklin Line

A Lincolnshire ploughman and his wife land at Mackay in 1883 on a free passage from Glasgow; an Irish couple keep the Queensland Hotel; a Gippsland dairy farmer's daughter writes a letter as the family pig. Six generations back on your mother's side are now on record — and "North" turns out to be a grandmother's maiden name.

Compiled 19 Aug 2026 Passes 18–19 Aug 2026 (three) Sources Qld BDM · Vic BDM · QSA immigration registers · NAA · Trove · FreeBMD · FreeCEN · Ryerson Cost $0 — free public records only

Two corrections this chart carries that the earlier record did not: Thomas Jacklin's mother was Maria Skipworth (his Queensland death registration's "Elizabeth" is wrong — one marriage, one wife, and Thomas and William were full brothers); and Langley Holmes was Fanny Margaret's stepfather — her mother was already a widow surnamed Holmes in 1861, and married Langley in 1868 when Fanny Margaret was nine. Her biological father is unnamed; a Bennet Holmes who married in Spilsby district in 1857 and died there in 1858 is the leading candidate.

Era I · Jacklin & Holmes

Lincolnshire — Keddington, Covenham, Bilsby, Louth, 1830 – 1883

c.1831
Abraham Jacklin is born at Keddington, a parish just north of Louth. In 1851, aged 21, he is an unmarried farm servant in the household of William Clark, farmer of 130 acres, Keddington. A1851 census HO107/2111A p.11 sch.31 (FreeCEN)
Jun q. 1856
Abraham Jacklin marries Maria Skipworth (b. c.1838 "Ashby", Lincs), Louth district. Confirmed both ways in FreeBMD's spouse cross-reference. This settles the "Elizabeth/Maria" contradiction: one marriage, one wife. AGRO 7a/1083
Mar q. 1857
Thomas Jacklin is born at Covenham, registered Louth. Louth is the family's "native town" of the 1931 obituary; Covenham is the birthplace both censuses give. AGRO 7a/560 · 1861 & 1871 census
Mar q. 1859
Fanny Margaret Holmes is born at Bilsby, registered Spilsby — the only Fanny Margaret Holmes registered in Lincolnshire 1850–70. AGRO 7a/528
Apr 1861
Census, Southfield, Bilsby: "Fanny Holmes, head, widow, 24, ag lab's widow", with Fanny M, 2, and a 71-year-old boarder. Fanny Margaret's father — a Holmes — is already dead. Same night, Great Carlton: Abraham 31, Maria 22, Thomas 4. AFreeCEN 1861 Alford piece 2378 ED9 p.17; Saltfleet piece 2385 ED10 p.107
Mar q. 1868
Langley Holmes (b. c.1844 Hogsthorpe) marries the widow Fanny Holmes, Spilsby district — a Holmes marrying a Holmes, both on GRO page 7a/797 the same quarter. He becomes Fanny Margaret's stepfather when she is nine, and is the "Langley Holmes" her 1933 Queensland death registration names as father. AGRO 7a/797 (both entries)
1871
Census: at Driby, Langley 27, Fanny 34, Fanny M 12, John J 7, Mary J 1. At Keddington, Abraham 40, Maria 33, Thomas 14 (already an ag lab), William 9 (b. North Cockerington), George 4 (a third brother, new). AFreeCEN 1871 RG10/3395 ED1 p.8; piece 3404 ED28 p.56
Sep q. 1878
Thomas Jacklin marries Fanny Holmes at Louth — five years before emigrating, not the "c.1880–83" earlier guessed. AGRO 7a/911 (both directions)
1880
Maria Jacklin dies, Louth, aged 42; Abraham remarries in the December quarter. By 1891 he is a railway platelayer in Eastfield Road, Louth, with second wife Jane A., tailoress; he dies at Louth in 1903, aged 72. BFreeBMD 7a/353, 7a/1161, 7a/337; 1891 census
Era II · Jacklin & Holmes

Mackay pioneers — the Hannah Landels, North Eton and Louth Park, 1883 – 1933

6 Jun 1883
The Hannah Landels, 1,400 tons, leaves Glasgow with 449 emigrants — 390 Scots, 43 English, 16 Irish — bound direct for Mackay. Aboard, on a fully government-paid FREE passage: "JACKLINE Thomas, 25" and "JACKLINE Fanny, 24". How a Lincolnshire farm couple got a free Glasgow berth to a Queensland sugar district is now the most interesting open question in the file. AQSA assisted immigration S13086, ITM18480 p.237, DR38564 · Daily Mercury 19 Sep 1931 (Trove 170403842)
11–14 Sep 1883
Anchors between Flat Top and Round Top on the 13th; register date 11 Sep; the ~350 immigrants landed at Mackay on the evening of the 14th. Thomas's first job: loading Mrs Mitchell's — Nellie Melba's — piano. Then farm hand at Eton Vale, North Eton, Barry Estate, Victoria Mill, "Pill Box", Farleigh; "one of the best ploughmen in the district". BObituary Daily Mercury 22 Oct 1931
1886–98
Four sons at Mackay: Thomas George 17 Jun 1886; Abraham 13 Aug 1890 (d. 20 Jun 1891); Abraham 9 Oct 1891; Henry "Harry" 21 Oct 1898. AQld birth index; C2681/1891
3 Jun – 26 Jul 1887
The Holmes family follows on the Dacca (not "Decca"), London → Brisbane, Captain Stone; "MACKAY — FREE"; county of origin Lincoln for all eight: Lang 41 & Fanny 48; John J. 23, already married to Ann 24, with Langley jr 2 and Florence 1; Mary 17; Tom 14. John Jarvis works 2½ years with his brother-in-law Thomas at North Eton, then farms at Woodford. AQSA ITM18484 p.170, DR38134 · JJH obit 26 Jun 1937
c.1890s
Thomas leases, then buys, at North Eton; freehold at Double Peak named Louth Park; supplies the North Eton mill in its first season; prominent rifleman. Not a Crown selection — no Jacklin in the selection indexes. BObituary · QSA land-selection indexes (negative)
1918–24
"Mrs Holmes senr" — Fanny — dies 31 Jan 1918 aged ~79 at daughter Mrs Harvison's, Woodford (registered as dau. of Thomas Grant Shepherd — a maiden name not yet found in any English record); Langley Holmes dies 27 Apr 1924. AC658/1918 · C1779/1924
13 Oct 1931
Thomas Jacklin dies; probate to sons T. G., Abraham and Henry, £3,249; widow living with son Harry. Death registration names parents "Abraham Jacklin & Elizabeth Skipworth" — the "Elizabeth" now known to be an error for Maria. AC3913/1931 · Daily Mercury 22 Oct 1931
24 Jan 1933
Fanny Margaret Jacklin dies, father recorded as Langley Holmes. AC577/1933
Era III · Taylor & North

Ireland to the Queensland Hotel — Wood Street, Mackay, 1888 – 1937

c.1863
Mary North is born in Ireland to Patrick North & Agnes Cooney; John Taylor, also Irish-born, to Robert Taylor & Anne Stokes. Counties unknown — the death certificates would say. AC4531/1937 · C4645/1925
5 Jan 1893
Mary North (arrived Mackay c.1888) marries John Taylor, farmer at Homebush, later Six-Mile. Children: Robert Joseph 1893; Ann Agnes 19 Dec 1894; a daughter 1896; John Henry 1898 (later Dr H. J. Taylor, medical superintendent Townsville, then Mackay); Mary "Tot" 1899; George Albert 1901; James 1905; Maria Avril; and a Mrs A. Phillips. AC1132/1893 · Qld birth index
1905–36
The Taylors settle in Mackay: John licensee of the Queensland Hotel, Wood Street, and proprietor of the Theatre Royal; Mary licensee 1915–36 (hotel demolished 1936); trips home to Ireland 1900, 1907, 1914 and 1932 (Eucharistic Congress, Dublin). John dies 2 Oct 1925; Mary 25 Jul 1937 aged 74, sister Mrs M. O'Neill of Marian. AQld death index · Daily Mercury
Era IV · Abe & Annie

Abe Jacklin — Eton, the Western Front, and the hotels of Mackay, 1891 – 1971

21 Feb 1916
"Abe Jacklin" enlists at Rockhampton (not Mackay), aged 23, born Eton, motor-car driver, Church of England; NOK "(Mother) Fanny Jacklin, P.O. Savannah, Eton". 5 ft 5¾, dark, brown eyes, black hair. 42nd Bn, A Coy. Embarks Sydney 5 Jun 1916 (HMAT Borda); France 25 Nov 1916. ANAA B2455 item 7361151, SN 1286
10 Oct 1917
Lance Corporal from 6 Aug; temporary Corporal 8 Oct; wounded in action — GSW right thigh — 10 Oct 1917 and reverts to L/Cpl on evacuation; rejoins 42nd Bn 22 Nov. (The press "Cpl. Abe Jacklin, wounded, Dec 1917" is this, via the notification chain.) A
26 May 1918
Gassed (mustard), France; invalided to England on H.S. Aberdonian; Horton War Hospital, Epsom, 7 Jun, cabled "SEVERE"; convalescent by late July. Transferred to the 15th Bn 5 Oct 1918, back to France 24 Oct. "Mr and Mrs Thos. Jacklin, North Eton, have received news … their son, Corporal Abe Jacklin, has been gassed" (Daily Mercury 21 Jun 1918). AB2455 · Trove 173907732
17 Jul 1919
Home: Port Napier to Sydney 4 Jul, then "returned overland last night … Lance Corporal Jacklin … and Privates A. and P. Harvison" (the Holmes/Harvison in-laws of Woodford), met by the Reception Committee. Discharged 20 Aug 1919. British War & Victory Medals; a Repatriation file runs 1916–1963. ATrove 178637688 · NAA BP709/1 M27236
30 Sep 1924
Abe, motor-car proprietor, marries Ann Agnes Taylor at St Patrick's RC, Mackay — best man brother Harry, bridesmaid "Tot" Taylor, Dr Taylor of Townsville Hospital the bride's brother. AC3285/1924
1926 – c.1932
Desmond John born 1926; page boy at his uncle's Taylor–Owen wedding Dec 1927. John North born c.1932, his middle name his grandmother's maiden name. A
1926–46
Licensee Albion Hotel Walkerston (to Nov 1926), Cremorne Hotel North Side (1927–29), 34/14 Gordon St Mackay (1933–34), Carmila (1935); "Jacklin's Flats, Gordon Street"; theatre exhibitor 1946 (Four Ways Theatre, Nebo Rd). Annie lives at the Queensland Hotel with her mother in 1931 (theatre-takings robbery case). 1941: nephew Paul Taylor (5) drowned at Seaview — reported by A. Jacklin of Gordon St. A
1962 · 1971
Abe dies 18 Mar 1962; Annie 19 Jul 1971 (QSA file 1972). AC823/1962 · C4873/1971
Era V · Ward, Cunningham & Spunner

Gippsland — Eddington gold, the Tambo River, Lake Tyers, Tambo Upper, 1855 – 1988

1855
Henry Ward marries Anne Byrns in Victoria; children Mary 1857 Prahran, Joseph 1861 Maryborough, Elizabeth 1865 and William 1867 Eddington (next to Dunolly), Henry 1873. Anne's maiden name is recorded variously Burns/Byrnes/Kavanagh; their own birthplaces unknown. Annie Josephine Ward d. Eddington 1887 aged 53. AVic 2918/1855, 14671/1867
c.1867
Thomas Cunningham & Margaret Murphy (b. Kiandra NSW c.1839, dau. of Andrew Murphy) "crossed the border in 1867 and settled on the Tambo River" — six sons and four daughters. Their daughter Catherine "of Swan Reach" is probably born around the move; she is not among the Victorian registrations 1872–88. CAge 9 Nov 1936 (Trove 205955071) · Trove 74169051
1895
William Ward marries Catherine Cunningham "of Swan Reach"; farms a selection of virgin bush at Lake Tyers. Charles William born 8 May 1895 near Cunninghame (Lakes Entrance); sisters Kathleen Annie 1896, Kathleen Mary 1901, Ellen 1904. AVic 5984/1895, 20047/1895 · NAA B884 V364966 (dob)
10 Aug 1907
Catherine Ward dies — the date comes from her son's own 1916 enlistment application ("Mother died Aug 10th 1907"). Yet no Ward death is registered anywhere in Victoria 1906–08 (71 checked), nor in any Gippsland district in 1907. She died, or was registered, somewhere else — NSW is next. A date · C whereaboutsNAA B2455 8347361 p.22 · Vic BDM API sweep
17 Mar 1916
Charles William Ward applies to enlist at Lakes Entrance, father's consent beside; attested Sale 21 Mar 1916, SN 2504, farm labourer, RC. 46th Bn from Dec 1916. Farewelled as "Pte Chas. Ward, of Lake Tyers" Aug 1916; embarks Port Sydney 7 Sep 1916. Trench fever, influenza, scabies; invalided to Brighton June 1918 with I.C.T. of the buttocks — never wounded (the Dec 1918 "welcomed home wounded Private Ward" was another man). Home on Anchises, Melbourne 13 Apr 1919; discharged 22 May 1919. ANAA B2455 item 8347361 · Trove 74176806, 74182543
1919
Charles marries Maud Frances Spunner (b. 1895 Kensington Hill, Melbourne; dau. of William Henry Spunner of Creswick, c.1865–1926, and Mary Ann Agnes Corkhill, c.1864–1903, dau. of Robert Corkill & Mary Ann Dwyer). Their eldest, William Charles, is born 14 Apr 1919 at Bairnsdale — worth checking against the marriage date. AVic 9907/1919, 30338/1895 · NAA B883 VX54353
Sep 1921
Discharged Soldiers' Settlement allotment, Tambo; "C. W. Ward, Tambo Upper" by Feb 1924 (medals re-application). Dairy farmer; secretary then vice-president Bairnsdale District Herd Testing Assoc. (best herd 1937); president Bruthen RSL to 1942; rural fire brigade; VDC 1939–45 (V364966, enlisted Bruthen). Children George Victor 1921–63, Mary Frances 1923, Margaret Elizabeth 4 Feb 1927. A
16 Nov 1935
"Pet Letter to Hamish" — eight-year-old Margaret Ward of Tambo Upper writes to the Sun News-Pictorial as Sally the family pig. Sunday-school concert 1933; gymkhana ladies' race 1944; bridesmaid at sister Mary's wedding to Clifford Roy Morrison, St Andrew's Presbyterian, Bairnsdale, 2 Dec 1944. ASun News-Pictorial 16 Nov 1935 p.2
1953 – 88
William Ward dies 18 Jan 1953 aged 85 at Picnic Point ("born at Dunolly … married Miss Catherine Cunninghame of Swan Reach … farmed at Lake Tyers"); Charles William dies 1962 Bairnsdale aged 67, months after applying to Repatriation; Maud dies 1988 Lakes Entrance aged 92. AVic 16064/1953, 22527/1962, 12303/1988 · Trove 269550302
Era VI · Desmond & Margaret

The doctor and the dairy farmer's daughter — Nudgee, Brisbane, Bairnsdale, North Mackay, 1926 – 2025

1939 – 48
Desmond: State scholarship 1939 (Mackay Centre); Nudgee College — high senior pass 1942, 100-yd sprint; MB BS University of Queensland, graduated Nov/Dec 1948; medical registration file 1948–50. ACourier-Mail 25 Nov 1948 · QSA ITM1659079
28 Nov 1951
Engagement announced: Margaret Elizabeth, younger daughter of Mr and Mrs C. W. Ward, Tambo Upper, to Dr Desmond John Jacklin, Mackay. Married 19 Apr 1952 at Bairnsdale. ADaily Mercury 28 Nov 1951 · Sun News-Pictorial 14 Dec 1951 · Vic 8334/1952
1953 – 55
Senior RMO / acting medical superintendent, Mackay District Hospital 1953; private practice at 73 Evans Ave, North Mackay from 25 Jan 1954; keen angler. Two children by Oct 1955 (Mrs Des Jacklin matron of honour at a Hobart wedding). ADaily Mercury · Telegraph 15 Oct 1955
Apr 1961
Brother North Jacklin — Nudgee 1947–49 (GPS high-jump and swimming records), Mackay SLSC beach-sprint champion 1950–52, Fields' Motors from 1951 — founds North Jacklin (BMC franchise), Mackay, with wife Judy; 60th anniversary 20 Apr 2021. A
1976 – 81
Desmond appointed a Commonwealth Quarantine Officer, Port of Mackay (Gazette 27 Apr 1976; appointment terminated Gazette 22 Jun 1982 after his death). Dies 9 Sep 1981; estate file 1981; his 1981 obituary is on Mackay library microfilm only. ATrove 240842173, 240545244 · Qld 56006/1981 · QSA ITM946943
1 Jul 2025
Margaret Elizabeth Jacklin dies, aged 98, late of Beaconsfield, Mackay; Newhaven Funerals NQ; probate notice 3 Oct 2025. Her notice body — which will name Judith's siblings and the grandchildren — is still to be captured. AMackay Funeral Notices 2025 archive · Ryerson Index

Lincolnshire origins · the big gain of pass 3

Keddington, Covenham, Bilsby: what FreeBMD and the census settle, and what they can't

The obituary said "native town Louth". The registers say a little more precisely: Abraham Jacklin was a Keddington man, born about 1831, a farm servant at 21; he married Maria Skipworth in the Louth district in the June quarter of 1856, and Thomas — the eldest — was born at Covenham in the first quarter of 1857. The family moved parish to parish as ag-lab families did: Great Carlton in 1861, North Cockerington for William's birth about 1862, back to Keddington by 1871, when Thomas at fourteen was already a labourer. Maria died in 1880 at 42; Abraham remarried within months, went to the railway as a platelayer, and died at Louth in 1903.

The Holmes side is a Spilsby–Alford story, not a Louth one. Fanny Margaret was born at Bilsby in early 1859 to a mother who, by the April 1861 census, was a 24-year-old agricultural labourer's widow. That mother married Langley Holmes of Hogsthorpe in 1868 — a Holmes marrying a Holmes — and it is Langley, the stepfather who raised her from nine, whom Fanny Margaret's Queensland death registration calls her father. John Jarvis, born about 1864 between the two marriages, is her half-brother; his 1937 obituary calling Thomas Jacklin "brother-in-law" is still right.

Thomas and Fanny married at Louth in the September quarter of 1878 and sailed five years later. Nothing on the free sites shows the household in between: FreeCEN has no 1881 Lincolnshire transcription, so whether they had English-born children who died or travelled with them is the single biggest remaining gap.

Solved

Maria, not Elizabeth. One marriage (Louth 7a/1083, 1856), one wife. Thomas's Qld death registration is wrong; William's is right; they were full brothers, with a third, George, b. c.1867.

Corrected

Langley Holmes = stepfather. 1861 census "Fanny Holmes, head, widow, 24" with Fanny M, 2; Holmes × Holmes marriage Spilsby 7a/797, Mar q. 1868. Biological father unnamed — candidate Bennet Holmes (m. Spilsby Sep q. 1857, 7a/837; d. Spilsby Sep q. 1858, 7a/328), a Hogsthorpe family name.

Not corroborated

"Shepherd" as Fanny senior's maiden name rests only on the 1918 Qld registration ("Thomas Grant Shepherd"). No Holmes × Shepherd marriage in Lincolnshire 1837–75 on FreeBMD, no Shepherd household near Bilsby in FreeCEN. Not refuted — FreeBMD's 1850s coverage is incomplete — but unconfirmed.

Also settled

James Jacklin "formerly of Gayton-le-Marsh" (d. Ipswich 1892) had parents George Jacklin & Theresa Walker — a separate Lincolnshire family, not Thomas's brother.

Two dossiers, forty pages · National Archives of Australia B2455

Your great-grandfathers on the Western Front

Both files were downloaded and transcribed in full. They confirm the family story on one side and quietly correct it on the other.

L/Cpl Abe Jacklin, SN 1286 — 42nd then 15th Battalion
Item 7361151 · 15 pp · Repatriation file BP709/1 M27236 (1916–63, paper only)
Enlisted Rockhampton 21 Feb 1916 — motor-car driver, born Eton, C of E, no prior service; NOK mother Fanny, "P.O. Savannah, Eton". Embarked Borda 5 Jun 1916; mumps at St Omer Jan 1917; L/Cpl 6 Aug 1917; temp. Cpl 8 Oct 1917 for three days; GSW right thigh 10 Oct 1917; furlough Feb–Apr 1918; gassed 26 May 1918, Horton War Hospital Epsom "severe"; 15th Bn Oct 1918; home Port Napier, discharged 20 Aug 1919. British War Medal 18863, Victory 18120. No disciplinary entries. Base Records sent his file to Repatriation Brisbane in April 1937.
Corrections: enlisted Rockhampton, not Mackay · substantive rank Lance Corporal · wounded 10 Oct 1917 (press "Dec") · gassed 26 May 1918 (press "Jun").
Pte Charles William Ward, SN 2504 — 46th Battalion
Item 8347361 · 25 pp · Repatriation file B73 M55544 (1916–86, paper only)
Applied Lakes Entrance 17 Mar 1916 (recruiting officer R. J. Gilsenan; father's consent "William Ward"; "Mother died Aug 10th 1907"); attested Sale 21 Mar; 20 y 10 m, farm labourer, RC, fair, blue eyes; birthplace "near Cunninghame, County of Gippsland Lakes". 19th Depot Bn Geelong → 5th Reinf. 46th Bn; embarked Port Sydney 7 Sep 1916; France 4 Dec 1916. Trench fever, influenza, scabies ×3; I.C.T. of the buttocks — invalided to Brighton 14 Jun 1918, Harefield, B1a4; one charge (out of bounds, Sutton Veny, 2 days CB); dermatological hospital Jan–Feb 1919; home Anchises, Melbourne 13 Apr 1919; discharged 22 May 1919. Medals re-applied for from "Tambo Upper" Feb 1924. Applied to Repatriation 29 Aug 1962, months before he died.
Corrections: never wounded — the Dec 1918 "welcomed home wounded Private Ward" (no given name) was another Lakes Entrance man; he had a pre-war cadet record despite answering "no". Confirms his mother's death date and DOB 8 May 1895 (WWII V364966).

What is not yet proven · and how to close it

Next steps, in the order that pays

Do these

  1. How did Thomas and Fanny get a free passage from Glasgow? The 1883 register has no native-place or nominator columns. Next: the Immigration Agent's correspondence and the Hannah Landels board/despatch papers at QSA; the Agent-General's emigration records, London.
  2. Find Catherine (Cunningham) Ward's death, 10 Aug 1907 — not in Victoria. Search NSW BDM (deaths 1907, surname Ward), then Qld/SA; try Victoria by place across 1907. Her registration should name Thomas Cunningham & Margaret Murphy and close the Ward line's biggest gap.
  3. 1881 census for Thomas & Fanny Jacklin and for Langley & Fanny Holmes — not on FreeCEN; a free FamilySearch account or a library day-pass will do it. Shows any English-born children before emigration.
  4. GRO index with mother's maiden name for Thomas Jacklin (Louth 7a/560) and Fanny Margaret Holmes (Spilsby 7a/528); and the certificate for the latter, which names her biological father.
  5. Who is on GRO Spilsby 7a/797 (1868) and 7a/837 (1857)? The page scan lists all four names — settles whom Langley Holmes married and whether Bennet Holmes is the first husband.
  6. Margaret's 2025 funeral notice body (mackayfuneralnotices.com.au / Newhaven Funerals NQ) — the fastest route to Judith's siblings and your cousins. And identify Heather Joyce Jacklin (probate 1 May 2026).
  7. Order Abe's Repatriation file NAA BP709/1 M27236 (1916–63) — 47 years covering the gassing and the family's circumstances.
  8. Lincolnshire parish registers (Keddington, Covenham, North Cockerington, Bilsby, Driby, Hogsthorpe, Louth) via LincsToThePast + FamilySearch images.
  9. Buy Qld death certificates C4645/1925 (John Taylor) and C4531/1937 (Mary North) for Irish counties; check the 1919 Ward–Spunner marriage date against William Charles's 14 Apr 1919 birth.
  10. Desmond's Sept 1981 obituary — Mackay library microfilm only (Daily Mercury not on Trove after 1954; Ryerson doesn't index it).

Dead ends and locked doors

  • FreeCEN has no 1881 Lincolnshire — the pre-emigration snapshot is unavailable free.
  • Victorian index 1906–08 — 71 Ward deaths, none Catherine; no Ward death in any Gippsland district 1907. Firm negative.
  • NSW BDM index — Cloudflare + Wicket form; couldn't be driven this pass. Next place to look.
  • Ryerson — HTTP 429 all pass; earlier capture reused. Desmond 1981 not indexed anyway.
  • Trove — no "Louth Park"/"Double Peak" farm items; no "Langley Holmes"; no Mrs Ward death notice 1907–08 in Gippsland papers; Daily Mercury stops 1954.
  • Land selection indexes — no Jacklin: Louth Park was freehold, not a selection.
  • Repatriation files (Abe BP709/1 M27236; Ward B73 M55544) — open, paper only, order or read in Brisbane/Melbourne.
  • Certificates — Qld, Vic, NSW, GRO all purchase-only; the indexes were used.
  • AWM embarkation rolls / Red Cross files — site not driven; low yield since both dossiers give embarkation and neither man was posted missing.
